articles.title: Trump officials scrutinized Omar in 2019. They didn't find citizenship issues.
articles.summary: Seven years ago, a political appointee in the first Trump administration approached U.S. immigration authorities with a request that alarmed career staffers: Scrub the immigration records of Rep. Ilhan Omar, then a newly elected Democratic lawmaker from Minnesota, for evidence of fraud. That 2019 demand, detailed by three former immigration officials, struck staffers at the time as a highly unusual effort to wield federal power to dig up compromising material on a sitting member of Congress who was a prominent critic of President Donald Trump. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. The request sparked a swift review examining Omar’s history, her family’s past as Somali refugees resettled in the United States and rumors that had circulated for years in conservative media over her marriage. Homeland Security Investigations - the investigative arm of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement - ultimately determined there was insufficient evidence of wrongdoing, one of the former officials said. The idea of pursuing a full investigation was eventually abandoned. Now, though, with Trump back in the White House and his administration using federal power to take aim at perceived enemies, Omar has once again found herself in federal crosshairs. She is now facing an inquiry over some of the same allegations investigators previously deemed not worth pursuing. The current effort - which burst into public view Monday as federal agents descended upon Omar’s D.C. home - is focused on whether she or her father lied on paperwork they submitted to obtain legal status and eventual citizenship after arriving in the U.S. in the 1990s. Investigators are reexamining questions about Omar’s birth date and her late father’s past military history in Somalia, which had passed scrutiny during the 2019 review. Depending on their findings, the administration could seek to charge Omar with a crime or move to challenge her status in the country. But such a step would be a sharp reversal of the earlier review, which found no issue with her naturalization, one of the former officials familiar with the earlier effort said. “I think her citizenship is solid and there wasn’t any fraud there,” the ex-official said. Omar has dismissed the revived investigation as yet another example of the Justice Department, under Trump, attempting “to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.” “Trump has spread lie after lie about the Congresswoman in a desperate attempt to justify his extraordinary abuse of power,” her spokesperson said in a statement Thursday. “This is politically motivated and an escalation of Trump’s personal vendetta against her lasting over a decade.” This account of the Trump administration’s current and past efforts to investigate and possibly build a case against Omar is based on interviews with a dozen people, many of whom spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss nonpublic details of those probes. Several current and former officials raised questions about the scope, tactics and motivations driving the current Omar investigation, which they say appears to be disregarding key norms on how immigration reviews are typically handled and bypassing guardrails intended to ensure federal inquiries, including those looking into sitting lawmakers, are not perceived to be driven by politics. A spokesperson for the Justice Department said the agency does not comment on ongoing investigations. The Department of Homeland Security referred questions to the Justice Department. Questions about the probe came into play ahead of this week’s highly public search of Omar’s home. Before carrying out the search, prosecutors spent days working to allay concerns from a federal judge that their plans could run afoul of constitutional protections shielding members of Congress from unwarranted executive branch intrusion, according to three people familiar with the matter. U.S. Magistrate Judge Matthew J. Sharbaugh, who ultimately signed off on the warrant, first imposed strict conditions on how the search should be carried out, the people said. His limits on the search appeared intended to ensure that the warrant fell in line with the D.C. court’s interpretation of the Constitution’s speech and debate clause, which generally shields lawmakers’ legislative duties and actions from criminal probes. As part of the search, agents removed boxes of documents and seized Omar’s cellphone and passport, one person familiar with the matter said. Trump has assailed Omar for years, and this week condemned her again on social media and public remarks. “I think she’s a terrible person,” he told reporters. “But that’s really up to the DOJ. I have nothing to do with it.” Trump’s administration has also made clear its scrutiny on Omar is not limited to immigration issues. Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney in D.C., announced Tuesday her office had launched its own investigation into Omar’s personal finances, tied to disclosure statements she filed in Congress last year and separate from the immigration probe. Pirro, a former Fox News host, once drew a highly unusual public rebuke from the network in 2019 for on-air comments suggesting that Omar, as a Muslim, could not be loyal to the U.S. Constitution. Omar’s office has previously dismissed questions raised by House Republicans over her financial disclosure statements as a right-wing attempt to “manufacture controversy.” However, federal prosecutors’ interest in the finances of Omar extend back to the Biden administration, according to two people familiar with the effort. Those individuals said it was not clear why the investigation during the prior administration appeared to have stalled. But the revived immigration investigation into Omar appears to be the furthest along and the administration’s higher priority. Alessandra P. Serano, an associate deputy attorney general who is playing a key role in the probe, went before the judge seeking the search warrant for Omar’s home, two people familiar with the matter said. Attorney General Todd Blanche also recently dispatched Serano, a trusted aide, to Florida to check in on the high-profile and struggling Florida-based investigation into former Obama and Biden-era officials, according to multiple people. Authorities have issued more than a dozen subpoenas related to Omar and the investigation into her, including some to her siblings, seeking testimony before a grand jury in Minneapolis in the coming weeks, two people said. The Washington Post has reported that investigators are focused on whether Omar or her father, Nur Omar Mohamed, intentionally misstated her birth date on immigration paperwork so she could be eligible to derive citizenship through him as a minor when he was naturalized in 2000. Investigators are also scrutinizing whether Omar’s father may have purposefully lied or omitted information on his past military service in Somalia that could have made him ineligible to obtain legal status in the country. But three former officials involved in the 2019 review of Omar’s immigration file said both of those issues were considered during that inquiry. An official with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, who was normally tasked with scrutinizing the backgrounds of people including serious criminals, terrorists and potential national security threats, was asked in 2019 to review Omar’s background. The then-freshman lawmaker had emerged as a frequent focus of conservative attacks. At the time, the agency was primarily focused on possible fraud related to Omar’s marriage to her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi. Right-wing commentators had repeatedly pressed unsubstantiated claims that Omar and Elmi were siblings who carried out a sham marriage so that Elmi could obtain U.S. immigration benefits. Elmi had previously filed an immigration petition related to his marriage-based green card that would move it from conditional status to permanent. USCIS requested additional evidence due to concerns over the validity of his marriage, but Elmi withdrew the application following that request, one of the former officials said. Elmi could not immediately be reached for comment Thursday. The 2019 review of Omar also looked at other issues, some of which are being examined anew. For instance, back then, USCIS quickly determined it could not accurately answer questions over Omar’s age because refugees frequently come from countries with little or no birth records, making it hard to determine with any certainty. “That’s not strange and that’s not a red flag to me,” one of the former officials said. “It’s just very, very common that there aren’t great birth records.” The agency also examined Omar’s father’s immigration file but did not find any issues, according to the former official. The USCIS officer tasked with vetting Omar produced a memo of those findings and shared it with a senior USCIS official and a fraud detention official before the effort was ultimately abandoned, the person said. Due to the sensitivity, the memo was printed out, and distributed in person, and not shared over email. Whether the current investigation will uncover more substantial evidence to back the administration’s fraud claims remains to be seen. Even if the Trump administration finds wrongdoing, any attempt to strip her citizenship would likely be lengthy and result in a legal battle. The administration, however, is also exploring the possibility that it could seek to revoke her citizenship certificate if the current investigation does not result in criminal charges or a conviction, a senior Trump administration official said. Revocation is a rarely employed USCIS administrative process that can be used to cancel the document due to fraud or an error. The process is not restricted to a certain period of time like criminal denaturalizations, which are subject to a 10-year statute of limitations. The revocation would not remove her citizenship but would make it challenging to obtain some government documents. This action could open the door to immigration-related charges and possibly removal proceedings, though such a novel application of the administrative authority would almost certainly face challenges from Omar in court. In a statement, Omar’s spokesperson assailed the Trump administration’s efforts to target the congresswoman. “He has lied about her family, about her immigration history, and about her love of this country,” the statement read. “But the truth is that Trump’s push to strip her of her citizenship and deport her has no basis in the law and has no precedent. This isn’t a legitimate law enforcement action.” Alexei Koseff contributed to this report. CORRECTION: A previous version of this article incorrectly described the length of a memo a USCIS officer produced about Rep. Ilhan Omar. The memo was several pages, not one page. articles.title: Oregon governor praises 'heroic' bystander who stopped school shooter
articles.summary: A teenager shot his way through locked doors at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore., on Thursday, killing three children and a teacher, police say. The children were 5, 8 and 11 years old, Bend Police Department Chief Mike Krantz said during a press conference on Thursday evening. The suspect, identified as a 16-year-old Bend resident, was shot and killed inside the school by a member of the community who saw him enter the building and pursued him, Krantz said. A 7-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were also sent to a hospital with critical injuries. The Associated Press on Friday identified the bystander who killed the shooter as Kyle Giamanco, a lifelong Bend resident and the father of two young daughters at the school. "He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel and community for the outpouring of love and support," Giamanco's mother, Kenda Freeman, said while reading a prepared statement to reporters outside her son's home near the school. President Trump on Friday called Giamanco a "great hero" who prevented the attack from being "much worse." "Thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it," he said. On Thursday, Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek praised the previously anonymous bystander for "heroically" intervening and stopping further loss of life. "Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well," Kotek said. Police did not release the names of the victims or the shooter. Krantz did not say what kind of gun the suspect used, although a law enforcement official briefed on the shooting told the Associated Press that it was a pump-action shotgun. Multiple outlets have reported that the shotgun was originally purchased by the shooter's mother, citing law enforcement sources. It was not immediately clear if the shooter knew anyone at the school or whether he had attended. Police haven't released any information about the shooter's potential motive. "This is going to be a long investigation," Krantz said. "We will have a large police presence at Silver Rail Elementary School for the next several days as our officers continue to conduct a very thorough investigation so we get all the answers. We appreciate your patience as we continue to investigate this terrible tragedy." The Bend Police Department has said it will provide further information at a press conference on Friday afternoon. How the shooting unfolded Flowers are placed beside a sign at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore., on Friday. AP Photo/Haven Daley According to an incident report posted by the Bend Police Department , Deschutes County dispatch received reports of an active shooter at 12:59 p.m. local time, from a person in a vehicle outside the school who said they had been shot at multiple times by someone with a long gun. The suspect entered the school after shooting through locked doors. Law enforcement officers were alerted at 1 p.m. and the school went into lockdown a minute later. Officers arrived at the scene at 1:02 p.m. "Seconds later, officers reported the suspect had been shot and killed, possibly by a bystander," police said. Officers then cleared the school, and all students and staff were transported to a nearby church for reunification with families and guardians. Federal law enforcement sources told Fox News that the bystander had a concealed carry permit. FBI Director Kash Patel said the agency was on the scene assisting in the investigation. "Our hearts are broken," Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler said during Thursday's press conference. "A school should be a safe place where children can learn and feel secure. What happened today should never happen." "We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy," Bend-La Pine Schools Superintendent Steven Cook wrote in a statement. "We extend our deepest sympathy to the families and to everyone affected by this violence. No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing. Our immediate priorities are caring for our students and staff and assisting law enforcement and emergency responders." The school district said all of its schools would be closed on Friday and crisis counselors would be available to to all students, families, staff and community members beginning at 10 a.m. at the Deschutes County Central Library. "We are all still in shock and starting to process the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School," Bend-La Pine Schools said in a press release . "We know it will take time to fully understand the depth and magnitude of this tragedy and how it will continue to affect our community." 'They're babies' People leave a family reunification area following a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore., on Thursday. AP Photo/Joe Kline Witnesses described hearing gunshots and seeing police swarm the school. "I heard what I thought was gunshots," Erin Johnson, who was visiting her parents next door to the school, told Oregon Public Broadcasting . "Then my neighbor began to scream shortly thereafter — her kids go to school there, at Silver Rail. Then I heard the police coming in." She added: "It's heartbreaking. I don't know any details right now about who was injured. But they're babies." Krista Johnson told OregonLive that she saw police swarm the school. "So many people stopping what they were doing," she said. "I knew that something had happened." Angela Nuchols told the Bend Source that she and her husband had dressed their 8-year-old daughter up for picture day before school, then raced to Silver Rail after hearing about the shooting. "It was crawling with police officers from all over the county," she said. "You've got guys in tactical gear, rifles. You're just scared to death wondering, is your child okay? You don't know." They were later reunited with their daughter. "It was like the worst three hours of our lives," Nuchols said. Thousands attended a vigil at Bend's Drake Park on Thursday night, many carrying candles, flowers and stuffed toys. "There is power and love in this park tonight," Kotek said at the vigil, according to OregonLive. "On behalf of everyone who lives in Oregon, I am so sorry for what you are experiencing today. No parent, no family, no community should have to have this kind of day." Kotek ordered flags at all Oregon public institutions to be flown at half-mast on Friday in honor of the victims. The Bend Education Association, which represents 1,000 educators in the city, released a statement emphasizing the work that will be needed to ensure that every student and teacher affected by the shooting has the support that they need. “When violence happens in one of our schools, it reaches far beyond that building,” the group’s president, Sarah Barclay, wrote on social media. “It affects our families, our colleagues, and communities across our country. Every student and every person who works in our schools deserves to be safe.” This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/multiple-people-reportedly-killed-after-shooting-at-oregon-elementary-school-230432197.html

articles.title: Kristi Noem no longer serving as Trump envoy to Shield of the Americas
articles.summary: Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem is no longer serving as the Trump administration's special envoy for the Shield of the Americas initiative, a State Department official said Thursday, though she remains involved in the administration's efforts to coordinate security cooperation across the Western Hemisphere. "Kristi Noem's envoy status expired last month and she is no longer in the role," a State Department official told CBS News Thursday. "She is now a senior advisor to Deputy Secretary Landau and continues to work on the Shield of the Americas portfolio." The Shield of the Americas is a coalition made up of the United States and several Caribbean and Latin American countries established by the Trump administration earlier this year to cooperate on economic matters, anti-cartel enforcement and other issues. In a statement on X, Noem said her role as special envoy "was always a six-month appointment." Noem's envoy designation expired just before the United Nations General Assembly last month in New York, where she continued participating in diplomatic meetings connected to the initiative. On Sept. 22, she met with Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa, whose government publicly identified her as the special envoy for the Shield of the Americas. She also attended a gathering of Shield of the Americas leaders hosted by President Trump, where he publicly acknowledged her work. "I want to thank Kristi Noem for doing a really terrific job," Mr. Trump said during his remarks. Noem was appointed special envoy for the Shield of the Americas in March, after she was removed as homeland security secretary amid mounting scrutiny of her management of the department and the influence of her adviser, Corey Lewandowski. Her transition to the envoy role coincided with a five-country tour of Latin America and the Caribbean in March, much of which took place as she completed her tenure as homeland security secretary. Lewandowski appeared in photographs during those visits, though the State Department later clarified he had no formal position at the department. Her public activities in the envoy role appear to have been limited, and included meeting Noboa in Quito on March 25, holding discussions with Ecuadorian and Colombian diplomats in Washington in September, and participating in meetings with regional leaders on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly. This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kristi-noem-no-longer-trump-envoy-shield-of-the-americas/

articles.title: Katie Zacharia reportedly out as White House press secretary after first week on the job
articles.summary: President Trump signaled on Friday that he might replace embattled new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia after less than one week on the job. Around the same time, multiple outlets reported that Zacharia had already been let go. Citing "three people familiar with the matter," the New York Times reported on Friday afternoon that Trump had "fired" Zacharia. A senior White House official told Fox News that Zacharia is "transitioning out" of her role, and CBS News and the Washington Post published similar reports. If confirmed, that would make Zacharia the shortest-tenured White House press secretary in U.S. history. "We're talking about doing something," Trump told reporters outside the White House, adding that he told Zacharia to "reconsider" whether she "need[s] this." "I told her, 'I think you're better off being happy and I don't think you could ever be happy in this job,'" Trump said. Asked if he was planning to "fire" Zacharia, the president said no. But, he added, "I want her to have a good life. I don't want [her] to have a life like she's led in the last three days. She is being brutalized by the media." Trump: "I told Katie that in my opinion she was treated very very unfairly by the news. Let's call it the fake news. I said, 'Katie, do you need this? I don't think you need this.' We're talking about doing something. I want her to have a good life. She's being brutalized by the… pic.twitter.com/Ivkk5imCjS — Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) October 16, 2026 Trump said he would discuss the matter further with Zacharia when he returns from a Friday campaign rally in Georgia. The president announced on Friday, Oct. 9, that he had chosen Zacharia, a conservative commentator and former Department of Homeland Security spokesperson, to replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the administration in August. Zacharia started at the White House on Monday gave her first press briefing on Tuesday. But she has spent the days since then facing questions about her own legal credentials rather than Trump's agenda. In his post on Truth Social announcing her appointment, Trump described Zacharia as an "attorney" as well as "a devoted fan and member of MAGA!" Zacharia holds both a law degree and a bachelor's degree from Pepperdine University, and her LinkedIn page says she served as "general counsel" at Fix California, a nonprofit founded by former acting Kennedy Center director Ric Grenell to promote conservative policies in the Golden State. In media appearances, she has repeatedly described herself as a lawyer. But the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that while Zacharia sat for the California bar exam after graduating from law school, she "didn't pass." A senior administration official confirmed to NBC News that Zacharia did not pass the California bar exam. Reuters also investigated her credentials and "could not find records showing Zacharia was registered as an attorney or member of the bar in any U.S. state or the District of Columbia." Asked by reporters Tuesday on the South Lawn where she passed the bar, Zacharia twice replied, "When I moved to China." In a phone interview with the New York Times on Wednesday , Zacharia said she misheard the question. "I assumed the question was, 'Where were you after law school?'" she told the paper.  "That's all I could hear over the sound of Marine One.  And, wanting to respect protocol, the distance behind the president, kept me from moving closer to hear the question." Zacharia pointed out that it was only her second day on the job. White House press secretary Katie Zacharia looks on as President Trump speaks to reporters on the South Lawn on Oct. 13. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson In a statement to the Washington Post , the White House said that "Katie moved to China with her husband after graduating because of his job at an American private equity firm while she worked on international transaction law." According to USA Today , Zacharia "worked for a Chinese law firm's international-practice team on multimillion-dollar shareholder agreements involving investments through the World Bank." She did not attempt to take the bar exam a second time. On Thursday, Zacharia confimed that she did not pass the bar, telling the conservative outlet Real America's Voice that she was "incredibly distracted and overwhelmed and excited" at the time by her impending marriage and move to China. "We just said… 'I'll take the bar and see what happens,'" Zacharia recalled. "The results are somewhat inconsequential because I knew I wouldn't need the bar in China." On Wednesday, a nonprofit watchdog group called Campaign for Accountability filed a complaint with the California bar asking it to investigate whether Zacharia had violated state law by "repeatedly holding herself out as a lawyer." White House spokesperson Steven Cheung responded on social media by dismissing the Campaign for Accountability as a "radical leftist-organization run by rabid numbskulls suffering from a severe case of Trump Derangement Syndrome." Legal experts told the Times that it's debatable whether a law school graduate can describe herself as a "lawyer" before she passes the bar. But she cannot call herself an "attorney" — someone who is licensed to practice law and give legal advice — nor can she serve as a "general counsel" or as an "associate" at a Chinese law firm, they added. Zacharia told Real America's Voice that she was "very careful about how I executed this and I never came across as somebody who was an attorney-at-law." "I consulted for a very long time many people in the field — 'Is it OK and acceptable if I label myself 'lawyer' … and provide legal analysis, not legal advice,"  she explained. "They said, 'Absolutely,' across the board. 'You can call yourself a lawyer.'" On Thursday night, Fox News host Sean Hannity pressed Zacharia on her halting explanation . "Why not just say, 'I went to Pepperdine Law School and then took a different career path, and I took the bar once and didn't pass it'?" Hannity asked. "Why get into this long drawn-out thing about the difference between a lawyer and an attorney?" "When I moved back to the United States, I didn't retake the bar," Zacharia said. "I had four kids in six years. It was never my intent to go into the practice of law." What happened in Zacharia's first briefing? White House press secretary Katie Zacharia speaks with reporters in the  Briefing Room on Oct. 13. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson Zacharia's first briefing lasted 15 minutes, most of which was taken up by her opening statement. "I am so honored to work for President Trump and the American people as the new White House press secretary," Zacharia told reporters in the Briefing Room. "I want to thank President Trump for his trust that he has placed in me. I have wanted to work with him for a very long time." She took questions from three news outlets — Breitbart, Fox News and the Daily Mail — before ending the briefing. Asked what she planned to do as press secretary, Zacharia said, "I get to do what I was doing on the outside already, which was getting to amplify, multiply and expand upon President Trump's incredible agenda for the American people." In his post on Truth Social announcing her appointment, Trump said Zacharia "has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning." Zacharia called the appointment "the honor of a lifetime" in a post on X . Who is Katie Zacharia? President Donald Trump and Katie Zacharia. Katie Zacharia/X The 42-year-old California native and mother of four left her role as senior communications adviser to Trump Media and Technology Group, which runs Truth Social, to join the White House. Before that, she served for about two months as a deputy assistant secretary and spokesperson for former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, according to her LinkedIn profile . She was best known for her frequent appearances defending the administration's policies on Fox News, CNN, Newsmax, One America News and other outlets. She told CNN in April — around the time she left DHS — that she's a "huge fan of ICE and a big fan of the Border Patrol." Zacharia first came to Washington in 2006 to intern for the Republican National Committee while George W. Bush was president. She lives in California with her husband and their four young children. During Tuesday's briefing, she was asked about juggling the competing roles of being a mother and White House press secretary. "The idea of not spending evenings with my kids is completely unacceptable," Zacharia said, before confusing her spouse with her boss. "So my president — excuse me, my husband — is out here." Zacharia then praised Trump as the "most family-friendly president we've ever had" and said her family will be moving from California to Washington, D.C., soon. CNN reported on Friday that Zacharia's "selection came about quickly" and that she "was not being considered for the role" as of "last week." CNN also reported that "on multiple occasions, senior officials had narrowed down the list" of possible press secretaries "only to find that candidates had said something negative about the president, disqualifying them from the position." In a New York Post column in February , Zacharia recounted a clash with liberal patrons of her "local cardio kickboxing gym" that ended with the gym owner asking her not to wear her red "Team Trump 2024" hat to exercise class. "I responded that I would never take my Trump hat off to appease the left," Zacharia wrote. "I refuse to stay silent." articles.title: ICE officer who struck man with vehicle put on leave as DA weighs charges
articles.summary: The Immigrations Customs and Enforcement officer who allegedly struck a man with a vehicle during a pursuit outside Houston last weekend has been placed on administrative leave, the agency said. The move is standard for all use-of-force incidents, according to an ICE spokesperson. "This incident is under active internal investigation," the spokesperson said in a statement Friday. On Saturday, Miguel Parra-Hernandez was hit by a car operated by an ICE agent during an arrest as the unidentified officer attempted to arrest him and another suspect, the agency said. Parra-Hernandez, who ICE alleged is undocumented, is currently in the hospital recovering from injuries to his legs, according to the Harris County District Attorney's office. Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare said Parra-Hernandez broke his leg in three places and has undergone two surgeries. KTRK - PHOTO: Law enforcement officials are at the scene after a man was struck by a vehicle driven by an ICE agent during chase, according to the Harris Courty Sheriff's Office, on Oct. 10, 2026, in Harris County, Texas. Parra-Hernandez has not been charged by any law enforcement agency as of Thursday, according to the DA's office. ICE agent strikes man with car during pursuit in Texas, authorities say ICE said in a statement that that one of its officers was pursuing Jose Mendoza-Cervantes, a Mexican national who they allege had a criminal record and a final order of removal by a judge, and observed him get in a vehicle with Parra-Hernandez Saturday morning. The ICE officer attempted a car stop, and Mendoza-Cervantes and Parra-Hernandez fled their vehicle on foot, according to ICE and the Harris County Sheriff's Office. Surveillance video of the incident reviewed by ABC News appears to show the ICE vehicle moving in the direction of a man running and then striking him. - PHOTO: In this screengrab from a video, a man is shown running prior to being struck by a vehicle driven by an ICE agent, according to the Harris Courty Sheriff's Office, on Oct. 10, 2026, in Harris County, Texas. An ICE spokesperson alleged in a statement that Parra-Hernandez "ran in front of an ICE vehicle" when he was hit. "Allegations that ICE struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez intentionally are RECKLESS and FALSE. The men and women of ICE are entrusted with upholding the rule of law and are held to the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, and ethical conduct," the spokesperson said in a statement Wednesday. Mendoza-Cervantes remains at large as of Friday, according to ICE. DA looking to interview 2 witnesses in backseat of ICE vehicle in Houston incident Teare, the DA, is currently probing the situation and told ABC News Wednesday that his office could possibly pursue criminal charges against the ICE officer. The DA's office said two people were allegedly detained by the ICE agent prior to the incident and in the back seat of the ICE officer's vehicle when Parra-Hernandez was hit. Teare told ABC News Thursday that his office was able to interview one of those witnesses before they were deported and that he believes the ICE officer intentionally struck Parra-Hernandez. "Thankfully, we were able to meet with him in custody yesterday, but we were the only individuals to even speak to him," the DA told ABC News. This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/US/ice-officer-allegedly-struck-man-texas-vehicle-administrative/story?id=137295824

articles.title: A powerful El Niño could disrupt winter getaways. Here's what travelers should know.
articles.summary: As travelers look to escape the cold for warm weather over the holiday season, an unusually strong El Niño could lead to unseasonal weather in several popular vacation destinations. The climate pattern, which occurs when waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, can shift weather patterns across the country, potentially affecting popular winter getaways from Florida to the Caribbean. "El Niños are associated with more storminess across the southern tier of the country, and potentially more ice storms across the southern plains," Matthew Rosencrans, a meteorologist at NOAA's Weather Prediction Center, told Yahoo. Those conditions can significantly disrupt travel, the meteorologist said, but the effects will be far from uniform. El Niño winters are also often warmer, Rosencrans explained, which can sometimes benefit travel across the northern tier of the contiguous U.S. Meanwhile, parts of the Caribbean may see drier weather, creating very different conditions for travelers depending on their destination. Where winter travelers could feel the effects Travelers heading to Florida this winter for a holiday getaway could face wetter-than-usual conditions, with El Niño increasing the likelihood of rainfall and severe weather across parts of the Southeast. "For Florida, it often means a fairly robust secondary severe weather season in November and into December across the Southeast and Florida," Rosencrans told Yahoo. NOAA's Climate Prediction Center outlook , released Oct. 15, gives the Southeast and Florida the greatest likelihood of a wetter-than-normal winter, with odds above 70% in some parts of northern Florida through the January to March period. Temperatures are forecast to be near normal across much of the Southeast. The winter seasonal precipitation outlook, according to NOAA. NOAA That doesn't necessarily mean travelers need to rethink a Florida vacation, but those hoping for uninterrupted beach weather should keep an eye on the forecast. While Florida could see a wetter winter, the Caribbean islands may see less rain, though it varies by island and time of year. "The Caribbean can often see drier weather during El Niño events, more strongly in the summer months from reduced tropical activity," Rosencrans explained. The ABC islands, Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao, are one example of where less rain is likely. Their main rainy season typically runs from October through January, with the dry season arriving later, from February through May. An El Niño suppresses that rainy season, according to the Meteorological Department of Curaçao . While lower rainfall over the islands may sound appealing, Rosencrans said it can mean fewer thunderstorms and make days feel hotter "as there is less cloudiness and continuous sunshine." Other islands show no clear lean either way. NOAA's winter outlook , released Oct. 15, gives Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands "equal chances of below-average, near-average or above-average seasonal total precipitation amounts" for December through February. Could El Niño affect hurricane season? El Niño has helped suppress Atlantic hurricane activity this year, but that doesn't mean the threat of tropical storms has disappeared. This year, Isaias became the first Atlantic hurricane of the season late on Oct. 7, making it one day shy of tying a 121-year-old record for the basin's latest-forming hurricane, according to the Associated Press . Lindsey Long, a meteorologist at NOAA's Weather Prediction Center, told Yahoo that wind shear linked to El Niño is still inhibiting storm development across the Atlantic. "In a typical year, we would expect about two additional hurricanes to develop between mid-October and November 30," Long said. By mid-October, the Atlantic would typically have had at least five, according to the National Hurricane Center , as reported by NPR . This year, Isaias is the first. However, the Gulf has been less affected by that wind shear and has extremely warm surface waters that could fuel storms, Long said. Formation typically shifts from the Atlantic's main development region, which stretches from the Caribbean to the African coast, toward the Gulf at this time of year. "There is still a continued possibility for tropical development throughout the remainder of the season," Long told Yahoo. The expert did add that a possible shift in when hurricane season starts or ends would not be connected to El Niño. Travelers heading to hurricane-prone areas may want to consider flexible booking options and review their travel insurance policies to understand what weather-related disruptions are covered. This article originally appeared on Yahoo Travel at https://travel.yahoo.com/advice/article/a-powerful-el-nino-could-disrupt-winter-getaways-heres-what-travelers-should-know-155951095.html

articles.title: Photos show Pope Leo celebrating Mass at the hospital after cancer surgery
articles.summary: The Vatican released new photos of Pope Leo XIV — the first since his lung cancer surgery — showing him celebrating Mass at the hospital in Rome. The photos, released Friday, show the American-born pope standing at an altar in green vestments, celebrating Mass at a small chapel in Gemelli Hospital. Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni said in a statement that the pontiff presided alone over the liturgy, distributed Communion to medical personnel and Vatican gendarmes present and delivered a homily. In his homily, Leo thanked the medical personnel for their service and their closeness to those who are fragile, and for the way they have taken care of him. The 71-year-old pope had a portion of his right lung removed and received a diagnosis of lung cancer earlier this week . He is expected to remain at Gemelli Hospital until Oct. 20. On Thursday, he resumed "a little bit of work activity, " including reading documents, and co-celebrated Mass, Vatican officials said. He also met with Archbishop Paolo Rudelli, undersecretary of state. Doctors said Friday that tests confirmed "steady improvement" in his recovery. "His post-operative recovery allows him to carry out his normal daily activities completely on his own," said a medical update signed by Leo's personal physician, Dr. Luigi Carbone, and the head of thoracic surgery at Gemelli Hospital, Dr. Stefano Margaritora. The Vatican said Leo spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin over the phone on Friday, during which he "expressed his deep concern about the grave humanitarian situation in the city of Oleshky" in Ukraine . Leo also called for a ceasefire to allow for food and medical assistance to be distributed in the region, as well as the safe evacuation of civilians. "The Holy Father reaffirmed the Holy See's commitment to promoting dialogue and peace," the Vatican said. The pope also held separate meetings with Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, the dean of the College of Cardinals, and Cardinal Baldassare Reina, the vicar general of the Diocese of Rome. The Vatican said Leo will make his first public appearance on Sunday to deliver the traditional noontime prayer. Past popes who have been hospitalized have recited the Angelus from the balcony on the 10th floor of Gemelli Hospital. Trip to South America appears still on Leo is scheduled to travel to South America next month. His ability to make the trip has been in question since his diagnosis, and the Vatican can change plans at any time. However, on Friday, the Vatican published the names of journalists accredited to fly on the pope's plane with him during his Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. Posting the media list signaled that, at least organizationally, the trip was going ahead. Cancer patients send well-wishing notes to Leo The Vatican also released photos of some get-well notes that had been sent to Leo from patients at Gemelli's pediatric oncology ward. One, from 7-year-old Angelo, told Leo that he had been on the 10th floor for 36 days. "My mother and I pray for you every night. Get well soon," he wrote, with little hearts at the bottom. Giorgia, a university-aged student, wrote to Leo in his native English, saying she had long loved learning and practicing the language. "When I heard on the news about you and your situation, I felt it a thousand times harder, because in some ways we're going through the same thing, and it made me feel closer to you," she wrote. "I pray to God that we both heal and I ask you to pray for me, too." This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/photos-pope-leo-mass-hospital-recovery-surgery/

articles.title: Fed chair warns AI spending could fuel inflation and pledges to contain prices
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh warned of a potential "shock" to the U.S. economy delivered by a rise in artificial intelligence spending , pledging to contain price increases as a flood of private sector funds drives up demand. "If you’re a central banker, you’re in the business of trying to ensure stable prices and full employment, you’ve got to recognize this as a shock," Warsh said in Bangkok, Thailand, at a conference organized by the International Monetary Fund. A surge in AI spending has helped boost the U.S. economy in recent quarters. In theory, an onrush of investment in activities like chip manufacturing and data center construction could put upward pressure in general on consumer prices, unless the demand is offset by a new supply of goods and services. Which grocery prices are rising the fastest and which are falling? "It’s obviously hitting the demand side of the economy before it’s hitting the supply side of the economy," Warsh said. Warsh, who took the helm of the Fed in May, has previously weighed in on the potential impact of AI on the labor market and wider economy. On Friday, Warsh reiterated his optimism about AI, saying the technology would ultimately generate added productivity and wealth. But, Warsh added, "the path from where we are to there is likely to be a very bumpy one." "We really don’t know what the market structure will be of these new technologies," Warsh said. "Who's going to be making the money?" Warsh acknowledged other shocks faced by the U.S. economy, including "shocks of war and military conflict." Eli Hartman/Bloomberg via Getty Images - PHOTO: The Nscale data center project in Barstow, Texas, Oct. 15, 2026. The outbreak of the Iran war in February imposed a historic oil supply shock and caused an acceleration of price increases in many countries. A U.S. government report issued this week showed inflation had climbed to a 4-month high in September as the Middle East conflict continued to drive up gasoline prices. Prices rose 3.7% in September, according to new data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics . Inflation stands more than a percentage point higher than the Fed's target rate of 2%. "It’s hard to be in a discussion with central bankers and not compare notes and hear the same thing about the surge in prices," Warsh said on Friday. He later added: "I’ve heard resolve from my colleagues around the world to deliver price stability. I’ve certainly delivered that resolve." Price hikes prompted the Fed to raise interest rates a quarter of a percentage point in September, marking the central bank's first rate increase since 2023. An increase to the benchmark interest rate aims to slash inflation by slowing the economy and eating away at demand, though the policy typically yields results after a lag time lasting several months. The next meeting of Fed policymakers takes place on Oct. 28, just days before the midterm elections. Gas prices set record for highest number of days above $4 a gallon in a calendar year Consistent with his approach in previous public appearances, Warsh opted against issuing a forecast about what the central bank may do at its meeting later this month. "I don’t pre-judge meetings. I don’t believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings we have over the balance of this year," Warsh said. Many investors appeared to interpret Warsh's posture as a sign the Fed may hold interest rates steady later this month. As of Friday morning, investors peg the chance of the Fed maintaining current interest rates at about 86%, which marks an uptick from about 55% on Wednesday, according to CME Group’s FedWatch Tool , a measure of market sentiment. This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/Business/fed-chair-kevin-warsh-warns-ai-shock-economy/story?id=137315708

articles.title: Major hurricane Trudy keeps strengthening as it nears Mexico's Pacific coast
articles.summary: By Aida Pelaez-Fernandez MEXICO CITY; Oct 16 (Reuters) - Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified on Friday, carrying maximum winds near 120 mph (195 kph), and is expected to ‌approach Mexico's Pacific coast as a major storm during the weekend. Additional strengthening ‌is still forecast before Trudy nears the coast of Jalisco and Colima states late on Saturday as ​a life-threatening major hurricane, Mexican authorities and the US-based National Hurricane Center warned. It is not expected to make landfall but will remain very close to the coast, about 60 to 65 km away, and any change in its path closer to shore will increase ‌the severity of its impact, ⁠the head of Mexico's weather agency Fabian Vazquez said at a press conference. "Everyone in this region needs to be very careful and ⁠stay alert over the weekend," he added. Mexico's civil protection agency asked residents to start preparations for the storm's arrival by securing doors and windows, and removing objects that could ​be thrown ​around by the strong winds. "Trudy has the ​potential to even reach Category 4 ‌or 5 intensity," said Alex DaSilva, a hurricane meteorologist at private forecaster AccuWeather. Located about 235 miles (380 km) southwest of resort city Acapulco, the storm is expected to produce up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, increasing the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, according to the NHC. HARD-HIT PACIFIC COAST The ‌hurricane will strike Mexico's Pacific coast, a region ​that has already been battered in recent weeks ​by storms that left several dead ​and caused severe flooding. "The most critical conditions will start on Saturday, ‌with very severe winds and waves ​along the coast, in ​an area that has already been affected for several weeks," Vazquez said. Tropical Storm Simon continues to weaken farther northwest offshore, after dropping heavy rain along the ​coast earlier as a ‌hurricane. Last week, tropical storm Rachel hit the Baja California peninsula damaging 1,500 ​homes, according to Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum. (Reporting by Aida Pelaez-Fernandez, Additional reporting ​by Raul Cortes; Editing by Toby Chopra) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/weather-news/articles/major-hurricane-trudy-keeps-strengthening-103029621.html

articles.title: 'You should be ashamed of yourself': Heated Senate debates become personal
articles.summary: WCSH Candidates faced off in heated debates Thursday night in two of the country’s most competitive Senate races , showing how bitter — and personal — each contest has become. In Maine, Democratic nominee Troy Jackson told GOP Sen. Susan Collins to “shut up” after she suggested a protester was one of his supporters. And in Alaska, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan questioned Democratic opponent Mary Peltola’s “character” while citing allegations she mistreated staff. “I think that Alaskans have had it up to here with the lying and dishonesty,” Peltola said during another exchange. “Dan, you should be ashamed of yourself.” The races are unfolding thousands of miles apart but both critical to the Senate majority. Collins, a moderate Republican, is seeking reelection in a blue state, while Sullivan is running for another term in more GOP-leaning Alaska where Peltola, a former congresswoman, is well-known. Both debates showed how much of a political liability President Donald Trump’s war in Iran has become for Republican incumbents. Sullivan said it “needs to end soon,” while Collins continued to insist Trump should have consulted Congress on the conflict. Here’s a look at key moments from the debates. US Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic candidate for the US Senate Troy Jackson are seen during their debate at the Gracie Theatre in Bangor, Maine on Thursday. - Charly Triballeau/AFP/Getty Images A protester disrupts Collins on data centers The fourth and final Senate debate in Maine grew heated as Collins and Jackson sharpened their attacks. Within minutes, a protester shouted at Collins about the impact of data centers, forcing the debate to a brief halt. “AI data centers are destroying our climate. They are poisoning our waters,” the protester yelled. Following the incident, Collins said the protester “is obviously one of Troy’s supporters.” “Oh, shut up,” Jackson replied, saying he did not know who the person was. unknown content item - Corruption allegations and campaign financing in Maine During the Collins-Jackson debate, both candidates tried to portray their opponent as corrupt, a major theme that has loomed over the hotly contested race and the midterms nationally. Collins cornered Jackson for not sharing his FEC report with her on Wednesday, a promise he made at their debate earlier this week. Jackson said he missed his self-imposed deadline because it took longer to process the donations from 200,000 people to his campaign than he expected. “I had to make sure this report was right. It was my first one,” Jackson said. Throughout the campaign, Jackson has framed Collins as being influenced by her donors and touted that he doesn’t take any corporate PAC money. Collins tried to flip the script on Thursday by dinging Jackson for running joint ads with his party’s Senate campaign arm, which does take money from corporations, and for not disclosing his donors. Jackson said he did not control their donations to the Senate campaign committee but did concede his campaign has taken money from billionaires. “That is accurate. But I haven’t made any deals like Senator Collins has with those billionaires. I don’t owe them any votes. I am going to tax those billionaires when I get to the US Senate. So, if they want to give me money during this campaign, I guess that’s up to them,” Jackson said. When it was Jackson’s turn to ask Collins a question, he got personal. In defending his credentials and pushing back on Collins’ critique that he doesn’t have the right experience, Jackson exclaimed, “Is it just me that you look down on or is it working-class people overall?” Collins further distances from Trump on Iran war Collins doubled down on her criticism of the Iran war as the Maine Republican continues to distance herself from Trump. When asked if Congress should have been consulted before Trump decided to go to war, Collins said, “Congress definitely should have been consulted.” But Collins added that that the War Powers Resolution gave Trump the flexibility to act unilaterally within the first 60 days of the conflict, which she said is why she did not start voting to rein in Trump’s war powers until after those initial 60 days had passed. unknown content item - Iran war’s consequences also hangs over Alaska debate Sullivan repeatedly had to grapple with issues where Trump has not made the race easy for him. The war in Iran, for example, has led to especially high fuel costs in Alaska. Sullivan said he has opposed limiting Trump’s Iran powers because he supports the overall goal of preventing the country from obtaining a nuclear weapon. But he said the war “needs to end soon.” “The energy costs from this war are too high, but … the best way to bring down costs with regard to energy in Alaska is to produce more energy by and for Alaskans,” Sullivan said, suggesting Peltola could not be trusted to support that. Peltola blamed Washington politicians for “waging forever wars that are skyrocketing our costs.” And she scoffed at Sullivan’s pivot to the topic of domestic energy production. “I have been a strong supporter of drilling in Alaska,” she said. “That is not the issue here.” Sullivan continued to show daylight with Trump when asked about Trump’s plan to buy Russian diesel . He reiterated his opposition, saying, “I don’t think it’s a good ideal at all,” and noting he “just led the effort” to pass new sanctions on Russia in Congress. Sullivan, Peltola spar over her treatment of staff Sullivan and Peltola clashed twice over a September story from The New York Times that alleged staff mistreatment by Peltola. In the article, her campaign pushed back on the suggestion she regularly abused her staff but said she occasionally “struggled to deal with her grief” after her mother and husband died in 2023. “I do not think that this election is about me on my worst day, and I found so many of these allegations concerning and outright fabrications or mass exaggerations of the truth,” Peltola said at the debate when asked about the Times report. Sullivan emphasized that the story was based on interviews with nine former staff members and at least 20 other people. “It’s not Mary Peltola on her worst day,” Sullivan said. “It’s Mary Peltola over the course of a couple years with dozens of people weighing in on this.” Sullivan brought up the Times story on his own earlier in the debate, saying Peltola has “treated young Alaskans horribly” and that it was “a character flaw.” Peltola called it “gossip” and “unfounded allegations” as Sullivan talked over her. “It’s the New York Times,” he said. “Read the article.” Sullivan questions whether Peltola got questions in advance The Times story was not the only cause for animosity between the two candidates. After Peltola criticized Sullivan about the war in Iran, looking down at notes on her podium as she spoke, Sullivan turned to the moderators. “We weren’t supposed to get these questions beforehand were, we?” he asked. “No, sir,” one moderator said before another added: “Neither one of you got questions beforehand. Absolutely not.” “OK,” Sullivan said. “I’m just watching my opponent read from questions that seem to be answered.” “I’m prepared,” Peltola said. Sullivan appeared to back down from his suggestion while speaking with reporters after the debate, according to Alaska Public Media , which quoted him telling the hosts, “I’m not blaming you guys.” This story has been updated with additional information. articles.title: 两党联手阻击特朗普松绑俄柴油协议！众院议案拟撤销豁免、强制制裁，布油盘中涨超3%
articles.summary: 美国总统特朗普放宽俄罗斯柴油出口限制的决定遭到国会两党议员集体阻击。 美东时间16日周五，美国众议院外交事务委员会的民主党首席委员Gregory Meeks提出一项两党议员共同支持的议案，拟撤销美国财政部已发放的相关许可、禁止未来继续发放豁免，并要求政府对俄罗斯能源行业实施制裁。这意味着，特朗普试图通过恢复俄罗斯柴油供应缓解能源价格压力、推动俄乌谈判的政策，正面临国会从参议院到众议院的连续反对。 以上议案消息公布后，国际原油期货在美股早盘尾声时段拉升。美股午盘之初，WTI原油期货一度接近每桶100.90美元，日内涨近3%；布伦特原油期货一度逼近每桶109.60美元，日内涨近3.5%。市场需要重新评估俄罗斯柴油供应增加的预期，以及美国对俄制裁政策可能收紧的风险。不过，油价走势还受到中东供应风险等因素影响，不能将盘中上涨完全归因于这项法案。 议案拟撤销柴油进口许可，堵住特朗普政府豁免通道 Meeks周五提出的议案名为《禁止腐败的俄罗斯石油交易法》（Prohibit Corrupt Russia Oil Deals Act）。据众议院外交事务委员会公布的公告及议案文本，该法案不仅针对特朗普政府当前的俄罗斯柴油交易，还试图限制美国未来通过一般许可放松俄罗斯能源制裁的空间。 议案的主要措施包括三方面： 撤销现有许可。 议案拟使美国财政部海外资产控制办公室（OFAC）此前发放的多项俄罗斯能源相关一般许可失效，其中包括直接涉及俄罗斯柴油销售、交付、卸货和进口的第135号一般许可，以及其他涉及俄罗斯原油和石油产品的许可。 禁止未来继续发放相关豁免。 议案拟禁止财政部继续发放相关一般许可，或授权实施其他原本受法律禁止、且通常为俄罗斯原油、石油产品、柴油和天然气交易所必需的活动。 扩大对俄能源制裁。 议案要求总统在法案生效后30天内，对参与俄罗斯油气开采、炼制或生产，以及石油和天然气海上运输的相关俄罗斯主体实施制裁，措施包括冻结资产和限制入境等。法案还拟限制美国国际开发金融公司（DFC）参与涉及俄罗斯能源资产的投资或金融安排。 此外，议案拟扩大国会对行政部门放松对俄制裁措施的审查权。根据提案文本，相关能源制裁放松措施将受到更严格的国会监督，直至美国国务卿会同财政部长、国防部长及国家情报总监向国会认证：俄罗斯已结束对乌战争，并可信地承诺达成公正的和平协议，包括赔偿乌克兰的战争损失。 这意味着，提案试图限制的并非只有当前这批柴油交易，而是特朗普政府未来通过行政许可恢复俄罗斯能源贸易的政策空间。 Meeks在公告中称，特朗普与俄罗斯总统普京达成的交易无法降低美国民众的生活成本，却会向俄罗斯提供资金，使其能够继续对乌克兰平民发动袭击。他呼吁国会采取行动，阻止相关协议。 法案获得多名民主党众议员联署，共同提案者中还包括共和党众议员Don Bacon，体现了反对俄柴油交易的跨党派立场。不过，两党议员共同提出法案并不意味着国会已经形成足够票数，也不代表法案必然通过。 参议院本周已两度施压，多名共和党人倒戈引关注 众议院的最新行动并非孤立事件。过去一周，特朗普达成的俄罗斯柴油交易已在参议院引发连续反对，且反对阵营中包括多名共和党资深议员。 本周一，部分两党参议员公开质疑特朗普政府放宽俄罗斯柴油出口限制的合法性，认为美国不应在俄罗斯仍持续对乌克兰发动战争之际恢复相关能源进口。他们要求政府撤回决定，并强调国会此前制定的对俄能源限制不能因总统的一项交易安排而被绕开。 本周二，反对声进一步扩大。据报道，12名参议员——其中包括6名共和党人——致信特朗普，要求撤销协议。他们认为，放宽限制将使俄罗斯能够更自由地向全球市场出售柴油，为普京政府继续战争提供资金，同时损害美国及其盟友的安全利益。 这12名参议员包括共和党人Mitch McConnell、Thom Tillis、Susan Collins、Alan Armstrong、Lisa Murkowski和John Cornyn，以及6名民主党人。部分共和党参议员此前也曾与民主党人共同发表声明，要求特朗普改变政策方向。 值得注意的是，特朗普面临的不只是国会对柴油协议的政治批评。路透社此前报道，特朗普根据上月签署的一项对俄制裁法律，需要在10月18日前决定是否对俄罗斯能源实施更广泛的制裁，或者以国家利益为由予以豁免。 因此，周五众议院提出新法案的时间点尤其敏感：一方面，国会反对者正试图通过立法限制行政部门的豁免权；另一方面，特朗普政府即将面对既有法律规定的制裁决策期限。 如果国会后续推进立法，白宫在俄罗斯能源问题上的政策选择将受到更大约束。但在法案正式通过前，特朗普政府能否继续依靠现有行政授权执行柴油交易，仍是接下来需要关注的关键问题。 从降低能源成本到对俄制裁，特朗普面临两难 特朗普的俄罗斯柴油交易原本被定位为一项兼顾能源价格与外交谈判的安排：通过恢复部分俄罗斯柴油供应缓解燃料市场压力，同时向莫斯科释放合作信号，推动俄乌重返谈判桌。 但过去一周的发展显示，这项政策的政治成本正在上升。参议院两党议员先后要求撤销协议，众议院又提出法案，拟从法律层面撤销相关许可、限制未来豁免并扩大对俄能源制裁。 对于特朗普政府而言，继续推进协议可能加剧美国国内的党派分歧，并引发对现行制裁法律执行方式的争议；若撤回协议，则可能削弱白宫通过能源贸易缓解供应压力、争取谈判空间的政策设想。 市场关注的也不再只是俄罗斯能够额外出口多少柴油，而是美国政府是否能够兑现此前的供应承诺，以及国会是否会通过新的法律措施改变交易的执行条件。 周五的众议院提案尚未成为法律，但它使特朗普的俄罗斯柴油交易从一项备受争议的行政决定，进一步演变为国会试图通过立法加以阻止的政策冲突。随着10月18日对俄制裁决策期限临近，白宫接下来如何处理俄罗斯能源问题，将同时牵动美国国内政治、俄乌谈判和国际原油市场。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 战略油储逼近纪录低位还要再动用！美国拟提供最多1700万桶原油
articles.summary: 美国战略石油储备（SPR）已降至1982年以来最低水平之际，政府仍在推进新一轮原油交换计划。 美国能源部于当地时间16日周五提出，拟向市场提供最多1700万桶战略储备原油，以履行今年3月国际协调释储承诺，并缓解伊朗战事冲击下的能源供应压力。 这并非一次简单的原油出售。按照交换机制，参与企业未来需要归还借出的原油，并额外交付一定数量的原油作为溢价。该计划可以增加短期市场供应，但也凸显出美国在缓解能源价格压力与保障战略储备之间的权衡。 此前交换响应有限，美国继续推进释储承诺 美国能源部此次供油属于一项交换计划，即原油以“借贷”方式提供给参与者，并在后续日期归还。交付时间为11月至次年1月。投标方须在2028年至2029年间将原油连同至少12.5%的溢价一并归还至战略石油储备。投标截止时间为美国中部时间10月21日上午11时。 美国能源部表示，本次招标采用“协商”方式，这意味着“政府可就原油交换数量、品质或本次招标的任何其他条款与投标方展开讨论”。 据报道，美国能源部此次重新征集原油交换方案，属于美国今年3月承诺从战略油储中提供1.72亿桶原油的一部分。当时，国际能源署（IEA）32个成员国一致同意合计向市场提供创纪录的4亿桶应急石油储备，以应对中东战争造成的供应中断。 不过，此前的交换计划执行并不顺利。今年6月，美国曾就相关批次征集企业申请，但由于企业需要归还原油并支付最高达24%的实物溢价，最终仅有约50万桶原油获得企业借用。 美国能源部仍在继续推进这项承诺。9月底，该部门还提出另一项最多涉及4000万桶原油的交换计划，显示美国正通过多轮操作向市场投放原油，同时要求企业日后归还更多原油，以补充储备。 战略油储处于1982年来低位，回补仍是难题 美国战略油储近年来持续受到关注。此前大规模动用储备，加上后续补充进度，令库存目前处于1982年以来低位。 美国能源部本周二公布的数据显示，截至10月9日，能源储备量维持在2.83亿桶，与前一周持平，战略油储（SPR）规模1.862亿桶，为1982年10月以来最低水平。距离该储备体系在里根任美国总统期内启用之初、即1982年8月的初始记录，目前的战略油储仅相差约1300万桶。 媒体本周稍早的分析指出，虽然美国战略油储近期库存企稳，但飓风相关的墨西哥湾供油中断等因素仍可能推动特朗普政府进一步动用储备。 原油交换与直接出售的区别在于，借出的原油未来需要归还，且通常附带额外原油作为溢价。美国能源部表示，这种机制既能在短期内向炼油企业提供供应，也有望增加未来的战略储备库存。 但交换机制无法立即改变库存处于低位的现实。随着中东冲突持续影响能源供应，美国继续动用战略储备能在多大程度上缓解市场压力，以及后续回补能否跟上，将成为观察全球原油供需和美国能源安全的重要变量。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 纳斯达克100站上关键支撑位，多空博弈进入决战时刻
articles.summary: 金融市场分析平台The Market Ear认为，纳斯达克100指数（NDX）正处于技术与基本面的双重考验之中。在经历一轮剧烈抛售后，指数在关键趋势支撑位和100日均线交汇处形成锤形反转K线，多空双方在此展开决定性博弈，若守住，可能触发强力轧空行情，若跌破，则市场或将急速恶化。 本周四盘中，半导体行业基金VanEck Semiconductor ETF（SMH）和内存产业基金Roundhill Memory ETF（DRAM）相关标的成交量暴增至近期峰值，多空对冲基金账面遭受重创，全球系统性多空策略一日下跌1.4%，接近四个标准差的极端波动。与此同时，科技股信用违约互换（CDS）利差持续走阔，信用市场与股票市场的压力信号罕见地趋于一致。 当前，NDX远期市盈率已回落至约21倍，重回2023年AI行情启动以来的估值低点。分析人士指出，随着仓位持续出清，进入财报季后盈利端或将成为支撑估值的关键变量。 关键支撑位：锤形K线与均线共振 据The Market Ear分析，NDX期货周四在自4月低点以来维持的上升趋势线上打出一根大型锤形K线，100日均线亦在同一区域形成支撑共振，令该位置成为当前市场的核心战场。 技术层面的逻辑清晰：若多方能够守住这一区域，此前遭受重创的空头仓位将面临被迫回补的压力，轧空行情的潜在力度不容小觑；反之，一旦支撑失守，缺乏有效承接的市场结构将使跌势迅速加剧。 信用与股票：压力信号终于同步 此轮科技股下跌的一个值得关注的变化，在于信用市场与股票市场的信号终于趋于一致。此前，科技股CDS利差曾出现一次明显跳升，但彼时NDX不跌反涨，令市场参与者困惑不解。 而本轮调整中，信用利差走阔与科技股下跌同步发生，两个市场"终于开始说同一种语言"。科技股隐含波动率指标VXN也随之走高，逼近9月高点，尽管从更长周期来看，波动率在过去两个月整体仍处于区间震荡，尚未出现趋势性突破。 半导体成交量暴增：止损出清还是再度去风险？ 本周四的抛售过程中，热门交易的标的出现异常放量。 当天，半导体行业ETF SMH和内存业ETF DRAM 均录得近期最高单日成交量，随后买盘介入，市场出现阶段性企稳。 高盛One-Delta交易台负责人Rich Privorotsky指出，多空账簿正在积极压缩总敞口（de-grossing），部分成交量可能反映的是被动止损平仓，而非主动的基本面判断转变。全球系统性多空策略昨日下跌1.4%，为接近四个标准差的极端单日表现，亏损的核心已不再是净敞口方向，而是总敞口规模——多头遭遇强力轧空的同时，空头也面临同等力度的逼空，双向杀伤特征明显。 AI资本开支：需求坚实，但结构性矛盾未解 Privorotsky对半导体板块的短期前景持谨慎乐观态度，认为AI复合体中杠杆最高的部分已从昨日低点出现明显反弹，信用层面的恐慌情绪在短期内或已过度定价，此处或为阶段性底部。 他提出一个潜在的相对价值交易思路：做空超大规模云服务商（hyperscalers），同时做多半导体。 然而，结构性矛盾依然存在。Privorotsky指出，过多资本正在追逐数量有限、具备电力就绪条件的算力基础设施，重定价过程远未结束，可能以渐进方式演进，也可能以剧烈错位的形式爆发，并向更广泛市场蔓延。 一个值得关注的矛盾现象是：尽管技术折旧加速，B200、H200、H100乃至老款A100的现货算力租赁价格依然保持强劲。这意味着AI融资端承压，但实际算力供给仍然稀缺，既有基础设施持有者的竞争优势短期内难以撼动。 收益率下行不再是科技股的护身符 自9月以来，NDX与美国10年期国债收益率呈现出罕见的同向联动——科技股与收益率同涨同跌，打破了“利率下行利好高估值成长股”的传统叙事框架。 这一相关性表明，当前主导市场定价的核心变量是增长预期与风险偏好，而非折现率本身。换言之，若收益率因增长担忧而下行，对科技股而言并非利好信号。 市场当前更担心的是增长放缓，而非利率水平。 估值触底：财报季或成转折催化剂 NDX远期市盈率已回落至约21倍，重新触及2023年AI行情启动以来的估值低点。 高盛全球银行与市场部美国TMT行业专家Peter Callahan指出，这一水平或已构成四重底的技术形态，为即将到来的财报季提供了相对有利的估值基础。 在仓位持续出清、情绪趋于极端的背景下，盈利端的实际表现将成为决定市场方向的关键。若企业盈利能够兑现预期，估值修复的空间或将打开；反之，若基本面进一步恶化，当前技术支撑位的失守将难以避免。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 长安管理层大变阵，朱华荣不再兼任上市公司董事长
articles.summary: 作者 | 周智宇 10月16日，长安公布新一轮管理层调整。朱华荣继续担任中国长安汽车集团有限公司党委书记、董事长，不再兼任上市公司重庆长安汽车股份有限公司董事长、党委书记；集团总经理赵非接任上市公司董事长，原常务执行副总裁叶沛出任总裁、党委副书记。 这轮调整中，一个关键变化是，集团总经理与上市公司总裁两个岗位分开了。此前，朱华荣同时担任两级公司的董事长，赵非同时担任集团总经理和上市公司总裁。如今，集团与上市公司之间保留赵非兼任董事长这一衔接，整车公司的经营岗位则交给叶沛。 其他调整也围绕两级班子展开。谭本宏继续担任集团党委副书记，不再兼任上市公司党委副书记；杨大勇升任长安汽车常务执行副总裁，邓承浩升任执行副总裁。克劳斯·齐乔拉转任全球首席高管顾问，不再担任副总裁、长安全球设计中心总经理。 这一安排距离朱华荣获选连任上市公司董事长不足一个月。9月17日，长安汽车完成董事会换届，选举朱华荣为董事长，并聘任赵非为总裁。长安方面解释，9月的选举是董事会期满换届，此次调整则是在新集团过渡期治理任务完成之后推进的制度性安排。 新央企成立后，长安需要处理的管理问题，已经超出一家整车公司的范围。 2025年7月，中国长安汽车作为新央企组建。集团层面要考虑整车与零部件、金融、物流等业务如何配置资源，形成怎样的产业组合。上市公司长安汽车则聚焦整车，要把研发、生产和销售组织起来，向市场交付产品，并对自身的经营结果负责。集团的产业布局与上市公司的产品经营，需要各有专门的负责人。 这次人事调整首先改变的是两级公司的兼职安排。赵非以集团总经理身份兼任上市公司董事长，集团战略和资源配置与整车业务之间的联系得以保留。叶沛担任上市公司总裁，承接的是将董事会确定的目标组织落实到生产经营中的职责。经营班子对计划执行和经营结果向董事会负责。 总裁从上市公司内部产生，让这层变化更为清楚。叶沛出生于1975年，曾任南京长安总经理、战略规划部部长、轿车销售事业部总经理，以及长安汽车副总裁兼乘用车营销事业部总经理，经历覆盖生产、战略和营销。与他同期晋升的邓承浩，此前已担任深蓝汽车董事长，长期参与新能源动力开发和整车项目。新经营班子主要从长安既有业务中接续。 这些岗位的经营压力，已经能从最新产销数据中看到。 今年前三季度，上市公司长安汽车累计销量169.27万辆，同比下降18.07%；其中新能源汽车销量70.93万辆，同比下降2.07%。按产销快报口径计算，新能源销量占比从去年同期约35.1%升至41.9%，提高约6.8个百分点。上述销量包含下属合营企业、联营企业。 新能源占比上升的同时，销量仍低于去年同期。这份占比提升中，也包含整车总量下降更快的影响。对负责整车经营的班子而言，提高新能源占比与恢复整体销量增长，是需要同时处理的两件事。 9月，长安新能源汽车销量同比增长15.64%至11.98万辆，但整车总销量仍同比下降19.11%至21.54万辆。当月海外销量9.42万辆，占总销量四成以上。新能源与海外业务都已足以牵动整车公司的经营，新班子面对的是国内外市场、不同动力和多个品牌同时运营的局面。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 拟增资逾21亿元，北汽蓝谷何时跨过盈利关？
articles.summary: 极狐与享界持续放量、毛利率转正，北汽蓝谷仍需要为日常经营补充资金。 10月15日晚，北汽蓝谷披露，拟与控股股东北汽集团向北汽新能源共同增资不超过16.38亿元；北汽新能源拟另通过公开挂牌方式增资扩股，引入外部投资者，增资金额不超过5亿元。两项合计上限为21.38亿元，主要用于补充日常经营流动资金。方案尚需股东会审议，外部投资者尚未确定。 这次增资发生在经营有所改善的阶段。今年前三季度，北汽新能源累计销量16.34万辆，同比增长46.52%；上半年，北汽蓝谷营收115.97亿元，同比增长21.86%，归母净亏损19.38亿元，较上年同期减亏约3.70亿元。 销量增长开始改善制造端的收益，但公司仍在承担较高的品牌推广和研发费用，销售收现也未同步增长。盈利改善与资金周转，是北汽蓝谷眼下需要同时处理的两件事。 北汽蓝谷已经通过极狐和享界打开了不同的市场，但两条产品线还需要形成足够稳定的经营回报。此次增资的意义，是为产品投入和销售放量提供资金支持。 更深一层的问题则是：当销量已经开始增长，公司如何让每一轮增长留下更多利润，逐步具备支撑下一轮产品开发的能力？ 01 增资补周转 此次增资的用途，直接指向日常经营周转。 其中，北汽蓝谷拟出资不超过10亿元，北汽集团拟出资不超过6.38亿元，另通过公开挂牌引入不超过5亿元外部投资。北汽蓝谷自身出资来源为自有资金或银行贷款，不含募集资金；增资后，北汽新能源仍纳入上市公司合并报表。 也就是说，21.38亿元中包含上市公司向子公司的内部投入，来自北汽集团和挂牌投资者的股权资金合计上限为11.38亿元。 对北汽新能源而言，资金进入经营主体，有助于保障采购、生产和交付。对于北汽蓝谷整体，最终效果则取决于资金能否支持产品持续销售，并带来更好的回款。 汽车业务的特点是，产品上市并不意味着投入结束。开发阶段要投入技术和工程资源，上市之后还要备货、组织生产、开展推广，并维持销售服务网络。车型越多，企业需要同时安排的资金就越多。 北汽蓝谷正在经历这样的阶段。公司上半年评估报告披露，极狐S3、享界S9焕新版等六款新品及改款车型按期上市，并继续推进后续产品开发。同一时期，公司完成约60亿元定增，募集资金按计划投向主营业务。 一位北汽新能源高管对华尔街见闻表示，下半年上市的这一系列车型，尤其是享界多款车型，是公司提升高端品牌销量与经营业绩的关键，称其“至关重要”。 从汽车行业看，扩大产品覆盖具有现实意义。消费者对价格、车身形式和动力类型的需求各不相同，单一车型很难长期承担一个品牌的销量。增加产品，可以覆盖更多用户，也能在部分车型进入销售淡季或换代期时，保持整体业务规模。 但产品增加之后，企业真正要解决的是如何提高既有资源的使用效率。一座工厂、一套开发体系和一张销售网络，需要有持续销量支撑。产品布局越完整，越有机会提高这些资源的利用率；如果各款车型销量分散、销售周期短，投入增加也可能快于回报。 这也是股东继续支持的产业意义。汽车企业从推出产品到建立稳定销量，往往需要跨越多个车型周期。资金支持有助于保持开发、生产和交付的连续性，让已经形成的产品能力获得更多市场检验，而不必因短期周转压力打乱经营节奏。 不过，北汽蓝谷眼下需要同时改善回款。上半年经营活动现金净流出17.50亿元，上年同期为净流入22.49亿元。公司解释，主要原因是销售商品、提供劳务收到的现金同比减少。 这意味着，收入增长尚未同步转化为现金回流。对车企来说，采购和生产需要持续付款，销售收入则要经过结算才能成为可用资金。随着业务规模扩大，回款速度、库存安排和生产节奏的重要性也会上升。 一位长期观察北汽蓝谷的汽车行业投资人向华尔街见闻表示，增资可以补充这段周转所需的资金。更长远的改善，则要靠生产与实际需求更好匹配，让车辆及时交付、货款及时回收。这样，增长带来的现金才能重新用于经营，而不必每次扩大规模都增加相应的融资需求。 北汽集团的投入也与外部投资者承担着不同作用。前者支持业务连续发展，后者还将检验市场对未来回报的判断。此次北汽新能源全部股权评估价值为359.34亿元，采用市场法，最终交易仍需经过挂牌等程序。 增资能缓解经营主体的资金需求，经营活动持续产生现金，才会进一步减轻融资压力。 02 最终都要落到利润 北汽蓝谷的经营改善，已经体现在毛利率上。 今年上半年，公司综合毛利率约4.21%，上年同期为负5.47%。按半年报数据测算，上半年毛利约4.88亿元，收入开始能够覆盖营业成本，并为销售、研发等支出提供一部分支持。 进一步看，这一改善并非完全依靠高价车型占比提升。兴业证券在近期发布的研报中测算，北汽蓝谷二季度平均单车收入约10.7万元，同比下降3.8万元、环比下降3.4万元，主要受价格带较低的极狐车型放量影响；同期公司毛利率升至约4.8%，同比提高约9个百分点，环比提高约1.8个百分点。该机构认为，销量增长带来的规模效应对冲了成本压力。 平均单车收入下降，毛利率却在提高，说明主流价位车型放量同样可以改善经营收益。汽车制造前期投入较大，工厂、设备和开发体系需要足够的产销量支撑。随着产量提高，固定成本能够由更多车辆分担，零部件采购和生产安排也有更大的优化空间。 这让极狐的作用更加清楚。今年前三季度，极狐累计销量13.55万辆，同比增长54.28%，仍是北汽新能源主要的销量来源。对北汽蓝谷而言，这部分增长既扩大了用户基础，也为提高制造体系和销售网络的利用效率提供了条件。 主流新能源市场的竞争，要求车企同时处理好价格、配置与成本之间的关系。车型需要有足够竞争力吸引消费者，也需要通过平台和零部件共用、生产效率提升等方式控制成本。二季度毛利率的变化表明，北汽蓝谷已经获得了一部分规模增长的回报。 接下来，这种改善还需要覆盖更大规模的经营支出。上半年，公司销售费用为15.13亿元，同比增长76.81%，其中广告展览费约12.94亿元。销售费用明显高于同期毛利，品牌推广和产品投放仍处于较高投入阶段。 但从单季度看，收入增长已开始摊薄费用。兴业证券测算，二季度公司期间费用约15.9亿元，同比增长约19%；期间费用率约21.2%，同比下降约2个百分点，环比下降约11.4个百分点。费用总额仍在增加，单位收入承担的费用则有所下降。 因此，北汽蓝谷当前的经营进展可以分为两层：公司综合毛利率已经转正，收入扩大也开始摊薄期间费用；但毛利水平仍不足以覆盖销售、研发和管理等支出，规模效应还需要继续积累。 对汽车企业来说，延续这一过程，需要车型在上市热度过去之后保持稳定销售。新品集中投放往往伴随较高推广费用，后续若能依靠产品口碑和既有渠道持续获得订单，就有机会在不同比例追加投入的情况下扩大收入。门店能够持续卖车，工厂能够稳定生产，前期投入才更容易转化为经营回报。 享界则为北汽蓝谷提供了改善产品结构的空间。通过S9、S9T等产品以及纯电、增程动力布局，享界让公司进入更高定位的市场，也扩大了能够覆盖的消费需求。 对于高端车型，较高售价为技术、配置和服务投入提供了更大的收入空间。其对公司盈利的贡献，取决于这些投入之后能够留下多少毛利，以及销量能否持续扩大。随着享界产品布局丰富，北汽蓝谷需要把高端市场的用户积累转化为稳定交付，再通过交付规模消化开发和制造成本。 上述汽车行业投资人士表示，极狐与享界由此提供了两种相互补充的增长来源。极狐扩大主流市场规模，有助于提高既有资源的使用效率；享界拓展高端市场，为改善收入结构提供机会。二者共同推动减亏的关键，是新增销量带来的毛利能够持续超过新增经营支出。 前期开发投入也需要在这一过程中逐步收回。上半年，北汽蓝谷研发费用约11.01亿元，其中无形资产摊销约9.85亿元，反映出既有开发成果等资产仍在持续计入当期费用。车型销售周期越长、累计销量越稳定，企业越有条件消化这些投入，并为下一代产品积累资金。 此次增资将为产品投放、生产和交付提供周转支持。对已经出现规模效应的北汽蓝谷而言，下一阶段的经营重点，是让更多车型从上市放量进入稳定销售，使工厂、渠道和开发体系持续获得足够的业务支撑。毛利改善与费用摊薄能否同步延续，将决定这轮销量增长推动公司减亏的速度。 风险提示及免责条款
